labels.NEW_PROVISIONAL_DESIGN: authorized joint-development rule in this revision; playable candidate only, not recovered canon and not independently human-playtested

waysToEarn: existing Expertise in that exact skill
lead two completed authenticated Equation-relevant findings using that exact skill from two different underlying evidence identities
advancedQualificationMark.earningPrerequisites: For each earned-finding route, the researcher must have the exact skill proficiency throughout every active interval used to resolve that finding. The finding must be authenticated and must answer a preregistered discipline question. Copies/duplicate observations of the same underlying receipt do not count as two findings.
advancedQualificationMark.note: The mark is qualification only; it never adds PB, Expertise, advantage, or a numerical bonus.

qualification.fullMatrixLead: At every active interval that requires Full Matrix Lead competence, the same individual must personally own all five Advanced Qualification marks and must currently possess proficiency in Arcana, History, Religion, Nature, and Engineering. Helpers cannot pool marks or proficiencies into one lead.
qualification.temporaryKnowledgeTransfer: Knowledge Transfer does not transfer marks, Expertise, memories, secrets, class features, spellcasting or tool ownership. It can, however, supply one currently missing skill proficiency for its actual one-hour duration. A researcher who already personally owns all five Advanced marks therefore qualifies as Full Matrix Lead during the loan window if that temporary proficiency completes the five required current proficiencies. Qualification ends immediately when the loan ends.

citations.excerpt:
## Ability-check skills

| Ability | Skills |
|---|---|
| STR | Athletics |
| DEX | Acrobatics, Sleight of Hand, Stealth |
| INT | Arcana, Engineering, History, Investigation, Nature, Religion |
| WIS | Animal Handling, Insight, Medicine, Perception, Survival |
| CHA | Deception, Intimidation, Performance, Persuasion, Reputation |

There are 20 basic skills; CON has no default skill. A Director can call for another appropriate ability with a skill when circumstances justify it. Use the reviewed [core task procedure](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md); attacks and ordinary saves remain distinct.

## Abilities and training

Ability modifier = floor((score − 10) / 2), including negative results. For example, 8 gives −1, 13 gives +1 and 16 gives +3.

**Optional new candidate method:** 27-point buy, scores 8–15 before ancestry. Costs are 8:0, 9:1, 10:2, 11:3, 12:4, 13:5, 14:7, 15:9. Spend no more than 27 points across six scores; no score outside that range. This adopts the existing companion method as a provisional option, not a claim that the book already specified it.

Resolve duplicate training as follows:

- For a selectable grant, choose another eligible option from that grant’s own list.
- For a fixed ancestry/background skill grant with no alternative list, choose another of the 20 basic skills.
- For a duplicated tool, choose another eligible tool from that grant’s list; if it has no list, use another actually supported tool in the same broad category.
- Duplicate armor, weapon, save or multiclass chassis training gives no skill or feat compensation. A new multiclass skill selection must still use its own permitted list.
- Duplicate proficiency never creates Expertise unless an exact feature says so. If a proficiency grant requires a choice and every legal option for that grant is already possessed, that grant provides no additional proficiency. Character creation, multiclass entry or advancement remains legal. Do not substitute a feat, Expertise, another category of proficiency, an unrelated skill/tool, or a banked future selection. This applies to skill and tool lists, including a legal replacement list or category that is itself exhausted.

PB is applied once to a check even if a skill and tool both qualify. An exact Expertise multiplier modifies that one proficiency contribution; it does not add another independent PB.

Ordinary spell research can be completed with Arcana and a laboratory. Matrix research cannot. The primary researcher must personally possess high ranks in multiple disciplines—Arcana, History, Religion, Nature, and Engineering—and must cross-reference rare drops, libraries, mechanisms, and seasonal changes. Archive knowledge may be inherited; cognitive continuity usually cannot.

value.name: Knowledge Transfer
value.effect: Knowledge Transfer. Tags: hero, spellbinder, knowledge. Choose one language you can speak or one skill in which you are proficient. The ally gains proficiency in that language or skill for 1 hour. Expertise is never transferred. The feature conveys functional knowledge, not memories, secrets, class features, spellcasting or tool ownership.

source.originalText: Knowledge Transfer: Temporarily grant an ally knowledge of a skill or language you possess.

value.name: Knowledge Transfer
value.disposition: KEEP Action,2RP,touch,willing ally,1hour,1/SR and no Expertise/memory/class/tool transfer. NEW language-mode cap: convey the donor's actual spoken competence and only the reading/writing/script modes the donor actually owns for that language, temporarily. Knowledge persists under ordinary current physical suppression but is not expanded by it.

4. **Choose one background.** Record its actual skills, tools, languages, feature and starting package, including required choices. Use the reviewed ancestry/background guide and complete source bindings for the20 background packages; its named outstanding interfaces remain outstanding. The source permits a custom background with two skills, two tools/languages, equipment and a Reputation-related feature developed with the Director; that permission does not supply an invented unlimited feature or a second background.

qualification.highRanksCompatibilityInterpretation: The Core phrase “high ranks” is not satisfied by five bare proficiencies. For this provisional interface, each discipline requires both current proficiency and its own Advanced Qualification mark when Full Matrix Lead competence is checked.

ordinaryFindingLead.requirement: For a bounded discipline finding, the lead must be proficient in that finding’s declared discipline for every active interval that requires that discipline. An Advanced mark in that discipline is not required to lead the finding that can earn it.
ordinaryFindingLead.scope: Ordinary authenticated subwork, observation analysis, provenance work, language-supported reading, discipline-specific finding work, and other bounded tasks whose preregistered question does not claim a complete Functional Model or Matrix execution authority.
ordinaryFindingLead.cannotDo: A discipline-finding lead cannot certify a complete Functional Model, Demonstrated Operational Understanding, Execution Attempt authority, or Full Matrix Synthesis merely because one discipline finding succeeded.

qualification.synthesisIntervals: The four-hour Matrix Synthesis requirement is 240 recorded active work minutes and may be paused. Each interval records start, stop, lead, assistants, current five-skill proficiency set, five owned marks, evidence set and clock conflicts. Every minute whose preregistered task requires Full Matrix Lead competence must be covered by qualifying competence. Incompatible Rest, recasting, travel, guard duty or other work does not count as active synthesis time.
qualification.oneHourWindows: Four genuine one-hour loan windows can contribute four synthesis hours only if each Knowledge Transfer activation is legally available and all actual costs, short-rest recovery, casting time and intervening world time are paid. Rest/recharge time never counts as synthesis time unless an exact rule expressly permits both activities, and the same elapsed minute cannot be double-counted.
qualification.languageEightHourBoundary: This pausable-interval rule is specific to the NEW PROVISIONAL four-hour Matrix Synthesis procedure. It does not modify, subdivide, shorten, or grant extra interruption permissions to the existing eight-active-hour Translate/Decipher project.
qualification.bardFeasibility: A legal Bard may choose Arcana, History and Religion from the Bard class list and may obtain Nature and Engineering from a Director-agreed custom background that uses the reviewed two-skill permission. This can create all five proficiencies, but bare proficiency in all five is still not the provisional “high ranks” threshold.

examples.text: A researcher proficient in History preregisters a chronology question against authenticated Library A evidence and leads a completed supported finding. Later they lead a different supported History finding from underlying evidence identity B. They earn the History Advanced Qualification mark; they did not need the mark before leading those two bounded findings.

A researcher copies and rereads two facsimiles of the same authenticated mechanism inscription. Because both derive from one underlying evidence identity and no distinct completed discipline findings exist, no Advanced Qualification mark is earned.

A researcher owns all five marks and four permanent proficiencies. Knowledge Transfer supplies Engineering from 09:00–10:00, so 60 qualified synthesis minutes accrue. At 10:00 the loan ends; continuing Engineering-dependent Full Matrix Synthesis is illegal until Engineering proficiency exists again.

After a legal short rest and a later legal Knowledge Transfer activation, the same researcher resumes the paused project. The earlier 60 active minutes remain recorded; only new qualified active minutes add toward 240. The short rest, recast and gap do not count toward synthesis.

separateRegisters.accessAndProvenance: Records what the party could actually inspect or observe, where/when, custody or source chain, authenticity basis, damage/missing content and underlyingEvidenceId. Possession is one possible access mode, not a prerequisite for knowledge.
separateRegisters.physicalCopy: Optional record of a facsimile/transcript/image/rubbing or other lawful copy. A copy retains parent underlyingEvidenceId unless it records a genuinely distinct observation event; copying never authenticates meaning and never multiplies corroboration.
separateRegisters.epistemic: Tracks what is supported: Literal Meaning, Authenticated Meaning, Supported Discipline Finding, Functional Model, Demonstrated Operational Understanding. These are not mandatory sequential ladder rungs.

evidenceStates.directComprehension: Accessible ordinary text in a language the reader actually knows may proceed directly to its literal meaning with no translation roll, subject to the current language rules. If provenance/authenticity is already supported, that text may support Authenticated Meaning without first making or owning a facsimile. An observed mechanism can likewise support a discipline finding or Functional Model through actual observation rules without a copy or translation when no text requires them.
evidenceStates.authenticationDefinition: Authenticated means the specific evidence/observation is supported as genuinely what the record claims it to be through provenance, custody, comparison, direct mechanism observation, a lawful identification procedure, or another actual source-supported basis. Authentication does not certify that every proposition inside a document is true.
evidenceStates.missingContent: No access, translation, copying, successful check or critical success reconstructs missing source content that the evidence does not support.
evidenceStates.duplicateCorroboration: Copies, retranslations and repeated readings of the same underlying content do not create additional independent corroboration receipts.
evidenceStates.categoryAccounting: A single real object/site can yield multiple distinct authenticated observation receipts when the preregistered questions, observed phenomena/conditions/times, and resulting facts are genuinely distinct. Each receipt records the same parent object identity plus its own observation identity. The same observation copied several ways remains one receipt and cannot fill multiple required evidence slots.
evidenceStates.antiGateLadder: No rule requires Possessed -> Facsimile -> Literal Translation before comprehension. Those are separate records used only when actually relevant.
rules: Functional Model requires supported cross-category evidence; it is not a complete recovered Equation, spell approval or execution authority.
Execution, Enforcement and Outside Enforcement are action records and do not retroactively create knowledge.

A distinct underlying evidence identity can support more than one discipline only when separate genuinely earned findings answer different preregistered discipline questions; the same statement or copied observation cannot be relabeled five ways.

functionalModelGate.antiInflation: No fixed fragment count. Evidence categories are not Equation pieces. Category receipts are authenticated observations/findings, not copies. One physical object may support more than one category only through genuinely distinct authenticated observations that satisfy different preregistered category questions; one copied observation cannot be multiplied across categories.

sourceBasis.excerpt: Ordinary spell research can be completed with Arcana and a laboratory. Matrix research cannot. The primary researcher must personally possess high ranks in multiple disciplines—Arcana, History, Religion, Nature, and Engineering—and must cross-reference rare drops, libraries, mechanisms, and seasonal changes. Archive knowledge may be inherited; cognitive continuity usually cannot.

value.decision: Research across multiple Descent libraries deciphers the Equation. Functional knowledge progressively taints/corrupts; greater understanding increases danger. Creatures at Descent level 5 onward can also be tainted by voices/proximity to the Old Ones. Causes are distinct; no arithmetic combination or threshold is supplied.

researchBlock.assistance: generic Expedition research assistance up to three trained meaningful assistants (+1 each) unless an exact subprocedure supplies its own assistant rule
researchBlock.clock: same world clock; incompatible work/rest/travel/guard tasks cannot overlap
researchBlock.resolution: Apply the current Core fixed-DC task degrees exactly after the preregistered DC/outcomes are fixed.
researchBlock.success: Certify the preregistered supported finding and its provenance/limits; never invent missing Equation text.
researchBlock.criticalSuccess: Certify the same finding plus only the preregistered additional corroboration/constraint that the evidence set actually supports.
researchBlock.failure: No certified finding; record the preregistered truthful progress result such as a narrowed conflict, excluded interpretation, identified missing receipt, or next legal method.
researchBlock.criticalFailure: Same truthful information discipline plus only a predeclared independently lawful hazard. It cannot create false lore or erase evidence.
researchBlock.retry: A retry is legal only after a concrete state change that could change the answer process: new authenticated evidence, a genuinely different supported method/tool/language capability, repair/recovery of missing material, resolution of a recorded conflict, or newly qualified competence. Merely rephrasing the same question, swapping synonymous wording, rereading the same material or adding an unauthenticated copy is the same attempt and cannot reroll.

citations.excerpt:
## Rolls

Choose the roll type before rolling. Use the actual ability modifier, including negative values, and normal proficiency only when applicable. Existing advantage/disadvantage chooses the higher/lower of two d20s; multiple sources do not stack, and any advantage plus disadvantage cancels. Add other legal modifiers once. Fractions round down unless a rule specifies otherwise. One tile is 5 feet. Class L, S and effect M retain their definitions in the shared class rules.

**Attack:** roll d20 plus the appropriate attack modifier against AC. Meeting AC hits. Natural 1 always misses; natural 20 always hits and critically doubles damage dice, not flat modifiers. Beating AC by 10 is not a critical hit. An explicit broader critical range does not stack with another; use the broadest eligible range. In this overlay, a natural result below 20 in that range must still meet AC unless the feature expressly says it always hits.

**Task, skill or tool check against a fixed DC:** total at least DC+10 is Critical Success; at least DC is Success; at most DC-10 is Critical Failure; other totals below DC are Failure. Natural 20 then improves one degree and natural 1 worsens one, bounded at either end. A task printing only success/failure collapses the two upper degrees to success and two lower degrees to failure; no extra consequence is invented. A natural 20 can still fail an otherwise impossible check, and a natural 1 with sufficient modifiers can still succeed.

**Saving throw:** total at least DC succeeds; otherwise it fails. Natural 1 and 20 have no generic special outcome. A printed failure by 5 or 10 compares the final total with the DC; it does not add an unprinted critical-save system. Death saves are the specific exception below.

**Opposed check, new provisional tie rule:** compare final totals. Higher wins; an exact tie leaves the existing state unchanged, so the initiating creature fails to change it. Do not turn task natural shifts into hidden numeric modifiers. A maneuver explicitly printing degree outcomes must specify how those apply.

value.title: Members, teams and offices
value.text:
An Expedition has at most **12 member characters**, including recruited NPCs and hirelings assigned independent Expedition jobs. Small Expeditions can use fewer teams and undertake feasible solo tasks. The following sizes are recommendations, not entry requirements.

| Team | Suggested members | Work |
|---|---:|---|
| Combat | 4–6 | Threats, battles and immediate protection |
| Reconnaissance | 1–3 | Scouting and mapping |
| Research | 1–3 | Study and identification |
| Resource | 2–4 | Gathering, crafting and harvesting |
| Support | 1–3 | Camp, care, repair and transport |

Appoint the five source offices: **Expedition Leader**, **Quartermaster**, **Routekeeper**, **Surgeon**, and **Claimant of Record**. The Leader represents the company and records tied organizational decisions; the Quartermaster tracks provisions, Load, cargo priority, wages and losses; the Routekeeper maintains the map; the Surgeon directs Wound treatment and casualty transport; the Claimant of Record maintains provenance, contracts and ownership documents. One person can hold several offices. An office grants no skill, extra Action or power over another player's consent or another owner's property.

Before work, record each member's primary activity or Rest, location, intended result, lead and assistants, and actual start/end times. Short tasks may follow one another. A person cannot perform incompatible activities during the same seconds. For a generic expedition task, up to three trained assistants who provide meaningful help each add +1. Exact crafting, harvesting, preservation, social and companion procedures use their own assistance rules instead.

Porters, bearers, guards and drivers contracted as members occupy roster seats. A public ship or caravan's external crew stays on its own service record and is not additional party labor or automatic combat support. Animals and source-bound noncharacter companions/devices do not occupy character seats; an intelligent creature recruited as an autonomous expedition character does. Larger forces use distinct cooperating Expeditions with real communication, shared finite resources and the same world clock.

citations.excerpt:
Plain accessible speech or text in a known language needs no comprehension roll. That does not establish its truth, solve a code, authenticate it, reveal technical context or recover missing facts. Remembering a specific message understood through temporary magic preserves that information after the effect ends; general competence does not persist.

| Task | Procedure | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Copy visible characters | Actual access, tools, stock and time | A facsimile; no certified meaning or magical encoding |
| **NEW** ordinary prose translation | Source reading and destination writing; ten active minutes per 250 words, proportionately rounded up to a minute, minimum one | Plain noncoded prose in the destination language; no roll merely for translation |
| **NEW** uncertain recognition | One minute; normally INT/History, DC 10 familiar attested style, 15 supported related form, 20 damaged but diagnostic evidence | Supported identity or relationship; no translation |
| **NEW** Translate/Decipher project | One preregistered supported passage of at most 250 words; eight active hours; declared evidence, method, output and DC | Only the supported passage or cipher layer |

Routine obvious recognition needs no roll. A nondiagnostic specimen cannot reveal its identity through a high roll. Translation speed does not replace formula-copying, magical encoding or contract-authentication procedures.

For the eight-hour project, register the actual source meaning or finite supported meaning, relevant parallel/grammatical/key evidence and missing sections before work. Linguistic reconstruction uses INT/History: DC 15 supported related dialect, 20 unfamiliar but adequately evidenced language, 25 damaged yet recoverable correspondence. A separate mundane cipher uses INT/Investigation: DC 15 adequate known key, 20 constrained ordinary analysis, 25 difficult but genuinely solvable damaged/incomplete key. A plainly usable key may remove uncertainty; it does not provide a missing underlying language.

Declare one lead and one applicable PB contribution. **NEW project-specific assistance:** one qualified assistant contributes +1 after all eight hours of actually useful participation. This does not add assistants to other procedures. Apply the existing Core task degrees and natural shifts.

Success supplies only the registered supported result. Critical Success grants no second passage, fluency, extra meaning, code bypass or banked labor. Failure leaves notes and spent work, without a certified translation. Critical Failure has the same informational result plus only a genuinely predeclared, independently lawful hazard. No failure fabricates authoritative lore. An inaccessible or unsupported meaning makes the project unqualified before work; a destroyed gap stays a gap.

A fresh attempt requires genuinely new evidence or a concretely different supported method, and fresh required work. Changing readers, dates, copies or formatting alone does not create evidence or reset an unchanged failed attempt. Information genuinely discovered can support later work; past hours and rewards are never credited twice.

Formula research and copying retain their trade gates, DC, minimum research time and one-hour/1-sp copying rule. Scribing Insight uses its separate procedure below. A subject-limited background information feature is not general translation. Pending research/language feats give no current discount or bonus.

## Communicate in a scene

difficultySelection.timing: Before the first active minute of the four-hour synthesis project, the Director records the exact research question, proposed supported finding, evidence identities/categories, lead skill, applicable proficiency/mark requirement, fixed DC, and all four degree outcomes. Assistants and known modifiers are recorded before the roll according to their actual rules.
difficultySelection.basis: Use an exact current procedure’s printed DC when one exists. If none exists for this new synthesis question, the Director selects a fixed DC from the supported difficulty of the evidence/question; the selected DC is part of this NEW PROVISIONAL procedure and must be fixed before work/roll rather than tuned after seeing the result. The Core fixed-DC degree procedure then resolves the check.
difficultySelection.recommendedBands: For this provisional synthesis interface only: DC 10 when the evidence directly answers a straightforward authenticated question; DC 15 when multiple authenticated records must be reconciled; DC 20 when the evidence is damaged/indirect but still genuinely sufficient; DC 25 only when the packet already demonstrates an exceptionally difficult yet solvable reconstruction. If the evidence is insufficient or nondiagnostic, there is no legal DC that lets a high roll invent the answer.
difficultySelection.noSecretRetargeting: The Director may keep the answer itself secret, but not silently change the preregistered question, DC or consequence table after the roll.
difficultySelection.fixedBeforeWork: Question, evidence set, DC, lead skill, legal modifiers/assistant rule, and truthful degree outcomes are fixed before the first active synthesis minute. No retargeting after seeing a roll.

researchBlock.authenticationRequirement: At least one cited access/provenance record must support each evidence receipt used. Unsupported rumor, an unattributed duplicate, or a copied claim with no provenance cannot be promoted to authenticated evidence by the synthesis roll itself.
researchBlock.distinctFindingRule: One underlying object can support distinct discipline findings only when each finding has a separately preregistered discipline question, distinct authenticated observation/meaning basis and independently supported result. The same sentence/observation cannot be farmed as several discipline findings by changing the skill label.

workedExample.title: Complete fictional qualification + synthesis example — demonstration objects only
workedExample.fictionalEvidenceDisclaimer: Every named receipt below is invented solely to demonstrate the procedure. It is not a recovered Equation fragment, holding, inscription, mechanism identity or canon site fact.
workedExample.researcher: Mara, a Bard, has Arcana/History/Religion from legal class choices and Nature/Engineering from a Director-agreed custom background. She already earned Advanced marks in Arcana, History, Religion and Nature. She has Engineering proficiency but no Engineering mark yet.

markWork.question: Does tooth count constrain the observed regulator ratio?
markWork.authentication: Authenticated observation with provenance record DEMO-A-PROV.

markWork.question: Does the authenticated residue support the same material-response constraint?
markWork.authentication: Authenticated distinct physical residue with provenance DEMO-B-PROV.

workedExample.qualificationResult: Because the two completed Engineering findings use two distinct underlying evidence identities and Mara was proficient in Engineering for all their active intervals, she earns the Engineering Advanced mark. She now personally owns all five marks and currently has all five proficiencies; Full Matrix Lead is satisfied. Bare possession of the five proficiencies before this did not satisfy high ranks.

project.question: Do the authenticated demonstration records support the bounded proposition that the fictional regulator changes response only when condition X and seasonal condition Y coincide?
project.categoryAccounting: One real object may support more than one genuinely distinct authenticated observation only when each observation has a distinct preregistered question/basis. A copy of any one receipt does not create another category receipt or underlying evidence identity.

predeclaredOutcomes.Critical Success: Bounded proposition plus the separately preregistered supported constraint that Y is necessary, if the evidence actually supports it.
predeclaredOutcomes.Failure: No certified proposition; record which evidence agrees/disagrees and the concrete next evidence need.
predeclaredOutcomes.Critical Failure: Same truthful informational result; only a separately predeclared lawful hazard may also resolve.

project.time: 240 recorded active synthesis minutes. Suppose Mara works 90 minutes, pauses for an unrelated interruption, then 150 minutes later under unchanged qualification. Only 240 active minutes count; the gap does not.
project.roll: Natural20 + Intelligence modifier 3 = 23 against DC15. Base degree is Success; natural20 improves one degree to Critical Success.
project.finalResult: Record only the bounded proposition and the preregistered supported Y constraint. No recovered Equation text, cosmological identity, execution permission, or Hunt trigger is generated by the check.

researchBlock.coreFixedDCTaskRule: For fixed-DC task/skill/tool checks: total >= DC+10 = Critical Success; total >= DC = Success; total <= DC-10 = Critical Failure; otherwise below DC = Failure. Then natural20 improves one degree and natural1 worsens one degree, bounded at the ends. A task that prints only binary outcomes collapses degrees as its rule says. Ordinary saving throws remain binary meet-DC/fail; natural1/20 do not generically shift saves.

predictionTests.procedure: Director presents three concrete outcomes derived from registered evidence. Player selects/explains from learned facts; use one existing-skill check only if uncertainty remains. All three successful/settled tests establish Demonstrated Operational Understanding.
predictionTests.failure: identify unsupported premise and create a research lead; preserve prior findings
predictionTests.episodeRule: Each of the three distinct prediction tests is its own concrete KT3 operational-commitment episode because each tests a separate preregistered proposition. At KT3, each can require one DC15 WIS Corruption-effect resistance save before costs. No reroll for continuing the same unchanged test after its transient Dazed ends.

taint.ownerBoundary: Functional knowledge progressively taints/corrupts; Descent level 5+ Old-One voice/proximity can also taint. Causes remain distinct. The owner supplied no stage count, arithmetic, DCs, durations or cure schedule; every stage/number/default below is NEW PROVISIONAL DESIGN and untested.
taint.candidateCorruptionClassification: For this provisional candidate only, the incoming influence that causes a KT3 resistance save and the incoming influence that causes a PT exposure save are mechanically identified as Corruption effects. KT/PT remain separate ledgers and are not the ordinary Corrupted condition. Corruption Ward may therefore grant its authored advantage on those qualifying saving throws while its one-hour ward is active. It creates no save where none exists, grants no cure/immunity/stage reduction, and does not affect the proposed PT recovery save, which is a recovery check rather than an incoming Corruption effect.

knowledgeTrack.trigger: No verified dangerous operational knowledge state.
First verified dangerous operational subprinciple: an authenticated supported finding whose operational relevance is explicitly established.
First supported Functional Model that materially connects multiple operational subprinciples.
First Demonstrated Operational Understanding: supported bounded proof that the character can predict/control an operational result under the adopted demonstration procedure.

taint.knowledgeEquivalence: KT follows actual supported knowledge, not paperwork. Equivalent verified knowledge acquired by another lawful route receives the corresponding KT state. Blind execution, accidental activation, rote action, Enforcement, or Outside Enforcement does not create understanding and does not advance KT by itself.

KT1 Resonant.pendingSymptom: After each completed legal long rest, create at most one pending KT1 symptom: disadvantage on the first eligible Intelligence or Wisdom Matrix-research task check made before the next long rest.
KT1 Resonant.consumption: The pending symptom is consumed by that eligible check whether the check succeeds or fails.
KT1 Resonant.grounding: Before it is consumed, 10 uninterrupted minutes of grounding clears that pending symptom. Grounding is deliberate quiet stabilization outside active Matrix research and outside qualifying KT/PT exposure, consumes real elapsed time, and grants no free rest/synthesis/translation credit. An exact rule may expressly permit another compatible activity.
KT1 Resonant.knowledge: No learned fact, mark, evidence receipt or KT history is removed.

KT2 Intrusive.postFailureAssistance: After a failed Matrix Synthesis task check, the researcher cannot provide or receive generic research assistance for 10 uninterrupted minutes outside active synthesis/qualifying exposure. This restriction has its own endpoint and does not erase findings.

KT3 Compromised.episodeDefinition: A KT3 operational-commitment episode is one concrete Demonstrated Operational Understanding prediction/control test or one concrete Hunt-capable operational-use commitment with a fixed intended operation/target/function. One save maximum per episode.
KT3 Compromised.saveTiming: Before paying the episode action/resource costs and after any required Hunt warning for a voluntary Hunt-capable commitment, make one DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. This save is a NEW PROVISIONAL DESIGN Corruption-effect resistance save for Corruption Ward eligibility.
KT3 Compromised.onSuccess: Proceed subject to normal action/resource/Hunt rules; no KT3 transient symptom from that episode.
KT3 Compromised.onFailure: Apply only the actual Dazed condition using CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST. Do not add a separate inability-to-decide, mind-control, reaction loss or concentration loss. The player may withdraw, or may continue when/if the intended action is legal under Dazed and all other rules.
KT3 Compromised.sameEpisode: When the Dazed symptom ends, continuing the same unchanged concrete commitment does not reroll. Pausing cannot manufacture another save or erase the episode.
KT3 Compromised.newEpisode: A genuinely separate later operation, new target/function, or separately preregistered prediction test is a new episode and may require its own save. Each of the three distinct prediction tests is its own KT3 episode because each tests a distinct preregistered operational proposition.
KT3 Compromised.immunity: Immunity to Dazed blocks the Dazed symptom completely. It leaves no unnamed equivalent decision prohibition. KT3 history and any separately legal Hunt commitment/trigger remain governed by their own records.
KT3 Compromised.huntSeparation: The KT3 save/symptom is not itself a Hunt trigger.

taint.proximityEligibility: Only Descent level 5+ and only an actual Director-declared qualifying Old-One voice/proximity exposure source/scene. Merely being deep, rereading a page, replaying one static record, or arbitrarily slicing one continuous exposure does not create repeated episodes.
taint.episodeIdentity: A PT episode is one continuous exposure to one declared qualifying source in one scene/continuous-contact period. Ten uninterrupted minutes outside that qualifying exposure ends the immediate episode. A later actual re-exposure can create a new episode; duplicate playback/copying of the same nonqualifying record cannot manufacture one.

defaultEpisodeProcedure.save: At first eligible exposure in the episode, make one Wisdom saving throw: DC12 at PT0, 13 at PT1, 14 at PT2, 15 at PT3. It is mechanically classified as a Corruption-effect resistance save for this candidate. One save per episode.
defaultEpisodeProcedure.onSuccess: No PT advance from this episode. Existing PT history and learned facts remain; the authored source may still have its own effects.
defaultEpisodeProcedure.onFailure: Advance one PT stage, maximum PT3, and apply only the new-stage endpoints below. Failure while already PT3 creates no PT4 and applies PT3 episode symptom once.

PT1 Whispered.nextCheck: Disadvantage on the next Intelligence or Wisdom task check before this endpoint clears. Consumed by that check or cleared after 10 uninterrupted minutes outside qualifying exposure.

PT2 Pressed.nextCheck: One next-check disadvantage endpoint exactly as PT1; consumed by that check or cleared after 10 uninterrupted minutes outside qualifying exposure.
PT2 Pressed.assistance: Separately, cannot provide research assistance until 10 uninterrupted minutes outside qualifying exposure. Consuming the next-check penalty does not automatically end this assistance restriction.

PT3 Saturated.dazed: Apply actual Dazed until end of the creature’s next regular turn in initiative or for 1 minute outside initiative. Dazed means Action-mode OR Movement-mode and no Bonus Action; Reactions and concentration are unaffected.
PT3 Saturated.assistance: Separately, cannot provide research assistance until 10 uninterrupted minutes outside qualifying exposure.
PT3 Saturated.noHiddenDisadvantage: PT3 does not silently inherit or generate an additional repeat next-check disadvantage unless another expressly applicable source imposes one.

taint.combination: Track KT and PT independently. Do not add stage numbers. Simultaneous actual effects use normal stacking; identical disadvantage never stacks. One cause does not rename or erase the other.
taint.groundingAndMitigation: Grounding/safe-exit ends only the transient endpoints expressly assigned to it. It never fabricates forgetting or deletes evidence, marks, KT/PT history or learned facts.

provisionalRecovery.KT: No automatic KT-stage loss from rest. Lower KT only through a later adopted rule whose real semantic scope lawfully changes the underlying dangerous cognitive state.
provisionalRecovery.PT: After one full legal long rest completed wholly outside qualifying PT exposure, make one DC12 Wisdom saving throw. Exposure before the rest began does not disqualify it; any qualifying exposure during the rest does. Success reduces current PT by one stage, minimum PT0; failure leaves it unchanged. Exactly one roll per completed qualifying long rest; subdividing a rest or counting one rest twice grants no extra roll. PT history remains. This recovery save is not an incoming Corruption effect and receives no Corruption Ward advantage from this classification.

taint.defenseAndCureScope: Apply reviewed defenses/cures by their actual semantic categories and timing. A rule need not print internal labels KT/PT/Hunt if it expressly covers the mechanically identified category. Corruption Ward applies only as stated above to eligible incoming Corruption-effect saving throws. Dazed immunity blocks actual Dazed. warningLadder.principle: A newly Hunt-capable voluntary action cannot rely on a warning that should have happened in the past. The mechanical warning is presented immediately before the first commitment point at which the character can knowingly choose a Hunt-capable action.
warningLadder.mechanicalWarning: Before commitment, tell the player in mechanical terms that continuing this declared action is Hunt-capable, that Hunt means hardcore status, and that an actual later death while Hunt Active normally becomes Hunted Death and blocks ordinary return. Do not reveal hidden cosmological identity or motive beyond earned evidence.
warningLadder.commitmentRecord: If the player deliberately continues after that warning, record the action’s commitment, actor, target/recipient, source procedure, timestamp, and trigger class. The warning itself does not start Hunt.
warningLadder.unforeseenAuthoredEvents: If an authored event is already resolving and the character had no meaningful choice before its Hunt-capable consequence became inevitable, do not retroactively fabricate informed consent. Resolve any authored unavoidable consequence exactly as authored; if the provisional Hunt rule itself requires deliberate continuation and none occurred, that event alone does not satisfy the deliberate trigger. If the event presents a choice window during resolution, give the mechanical warning before that choice closes.
warningLadder.noFreeImmunity: Lack of an old warning record does not permanently immunize a character. The Director supplies the warning at the next legal commitment point before a Hunt-capable voluntary act.

citations.excerpt: Infernal powers trade in soul coins, bargains, resurrection clauses, and contracts written to remain enforceable even after the dungeon seals.

Conclave agreed to pilot program in Avernus front lines. Soul Warden Innorbatos presented charter to legion deserters, offering protection in exchange for eternal service with explicit statement that freedom never regained. Some accepted, seeing offer as honest anchor in chaotic war. When charter sealed, lattice pulsed, not in condemnation, but with somber note, recognizing authentic submission. Devils exulted until vision revealed souls glowing dim, energy yield lower than deceit harvested souls. Asmodeus realised sincerity curbed despair, reducing nutritional value for Hell. Plan considered unsustainable. Simultaneously Crimson Accord shuddered. Demons sensed devils flirting with authenticity and erupted in outrage, for chaos realm defines itself by rejection of coherent narrative. Ul nak stirred in distant dream, whispering through Abyssal storms, promising power to any legion that shattered lattice. Tanar ri warbands swarmed infernal border, screaming truths of raw impulse, blades coated with madness. The sentient Pact responded by wrapping battlefield with shimmering veil that manifested each combatant true desire as visible flame trailing movements. Soldiers saw own motive writ large, fear or lust or hatred or love. Some halted, disgusted. Others fought harder, proud of flame. Casualty patterns shifted unpredictably.

operational.limitations: An already-living identity is ineligible. Lethal tracks and persistent afflictions remain; apply their reviewed reconciliation rather than silently removing them. Refusal or a counter after a legal paid activation refunds nothing. # Time Loop: reviewed foundational transaction kernel

**Status: REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED within the bounded foundational scope. Full Time Loop remains unavailable.**

**Current-file qualification:** the original approval binds helper hash `b821829ed352e69ce1ecf3c3d753f0206c8f8d2ec5a5d64bc89d5fd7d8a72151`, preserved as `docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/temporal_playtest_rules_reviewed_foundation.py` at the game root. The current helper adds a control/pulse transaction adapter and regular-start phase tracking. Those extensions are now covered by the separate [bounded control/pulse review manifest](TEMPORAL_CONTROL_WORLD_REVIEW_STATUS.json), following actual notebook confirmation. They do not inherit the historical approval. The 76 foundation regressions still pass. See [integration progress](TEMPORAL_CONTROL_PLAYTEST.md).

This implements a bounded part of `oracle.supplement.spiral-touched.spiral-touched-boon-v`. It does not change the original source, enable the ability in the playable class catalog, or close the full temporal interface. The notebook's twelve decisions are the authority for this candidate: [boundary conference](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_WORLD_BOUNDARIES.md).

## What is implemented

The reference restores an immutable initiative-start snapshot through a preflighted transaction. It handles a finite development scene containing canonical Core life states, action wallets, selected feat shields, a temporal healing-consumption ledger, explicit Soul Bind/death identities, physical provenance, finite level-ground geometry, reward opportunities, external dependency records and character memory. The existing shared `LifeState`, `Wallet` and `BufferLedger` objects retain their identities. Spent resources and historical event records remain current.

The restore is permitted only after a complete atomic combat event, before round four, with an available Reaction and an unspent actual long-rest use. It never interrupts a damage, healing or command transaction. Preflight checks all registered state, source policies, physical dependencies and placements before charging anything. A prepared plan becomes stale if the registered world changes before commit. The single-thread reference requires the host scene lock through preflight and commit. Each committed restore also retains an engine/Director audit frame with the previous and resulting field values; that audit is never a source of character memory. The existing canonical BufferLedger completed-rest epoch also governs Time Loop's own long-rest use; there is no independent rest counter to diverge.

At commit, encounter initiative and the snapshot's Action/Bonus Action/Reaction allowances, RC and declared per-encounter uses return. Every outstanding Oracle Time Loop Reaction debt overlays the restored budgets. Only the owner's actual normal regular-start refresh clears that owner's debt. The public `TemporalKernel.regular_start(actor, now)` obtains the actor's canonical Wallet internally; it accepts no Wallet argument and rejects actor aliases sharing one Wallet. The bounded scheduler enforces the next actor at the initiative cursor, allows one active regular turn, and advances the cursor/round only when that exact turn ends. An out-of-order or repeated start cannot refresh a Reaction or advance the actual regular marker. Genuine extra turns require the later source adapter and cannot be represented as regular starts. The new iteration has fresh round/turn identities; the rewind itself creates no turn start, pulse or recharge tick. Elapsed world time, real regular-marker count, RP and finite-use history remain unchanged.

## Conservation checks

| State | Bounded behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Core HP and Wounds | Restore numeric snapshot HP against the current legal maximum. A lower maximum clamps HP without damage or healing; a higher maximum does not increase snapshot HP. Critical Wound healing ceilings do not limit temporal assignment. |
| Maximum HP | Use the existing maximum-HP calculation and an exact source-ID temporal policy table. The three reviewed Monk trauma IDs may restore except after actual rest ending. Tough, Tough as Nails, Tenacity and Dark Fortitude use current permanent progression records; temporary endpoints on those passive records are rejected. Other sources, including valid ordinary max-HP sources whose temporal/lifecycle adapter is absent, reject this fixture. Current supported external records overlay the result. Structural progression changes reject without a dedicated adapter. The host supplies current legal base/stat values. |
| Stable recovery | Preserve its original world deadline and event identity. An already resolved or expired recovery cannot replay; this kernel rejects such restoration rather than inventing a recovery rule. |
| Temporary HP | Restore the same grant ID and original snapshot amount only while its source's deadline/rest epoch/entity dependency remains valid. Supported IDs are Chef, Inspiring Leader, Field Medic, Soul Cage, Empowered Summoning and Blood Ritual. Required canonical ledger fields, unique grant IDs, active target/state and positive remaining amount are validated. Unknown sources and linked riders reject the scene. |
| One-shot healing reduction | Keep canonical effect ID and all past events. Consumption keys include the iteration. Snapshot-available Agony can be available in a new iteration before its original expiry; snapshot-consumed or expired Agony remains unavailable. |
| Soul Bind | Original absolute deadline, exact death instance for bound-dead records. An active pending record requires a living, non-Stable, dying zero-HP target with no death-instance binding. Application and target identities must match. Undoing a later death removes that later active bind. No revival event or source cost is manufactured. |
| Rewards | A claim belongs to encounter origin, immutable reward source, opportunity kind and source-defined slot. Another death event or iteration cannot make another claim. |
| Physical derivatives | Traverse immutable provenance transitively. A wholly in-scope, reversible temporal entity can retire; its costs stay spent. Surviving harvested inventory, mixed material roots, external source slots or persistent enrollment conflicts block the restore. Already consumed material remains consumed. |
| Outsiders | Keep body state, inventory ownership, resource history and concentration records. A snapshot dependency must still exist exactly and refer to the same live concentration ID. New current dependencies targeting restored participants need a supported overlay; otherwise they block. Unimplemented external anatomy/control/suppression overlays also block. |
| Environment | Each anchor has an exact canonical physical identity. Restore snapshot environment existence together with its geometry; remove both the physical derivative and its geometry when retiring a later temporal entity. Plan all participant positions simultaneously. Reject overlap, loss of support, and restrictions to a protected outsider's previously reachable ground area. This is deliberately limited to a finite orthogonal level ground plane, not flying, elevation, portals or mandatory growth. |
| Memory | The invoking Oracle and their immutable snapshot allies retain only facts individually perceived, experienced or received. Retained memories accumulate across loops. Enemy player characters receive no special knowledge; no hidden roster or Director facts enter memory automatically. |

## What the agreed rules mean at the table

These examples explain the reviewed boundaries. They do not enable the full ability before its remaining integrations are complete.

| Situation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| At initiative, an ally has25HP. Later they fall to3HP and spend8RP. Time Loop succeeds. | They return to25HP, limited by their current legal maximum. The8RP remain spent. Their snapshot encounter allowances return where the source explicitly permits it. |
| The same ally's legal maximum has fallen to20 because a conserved source changed. | They return to20HP. The reduction is temporal normalization, not damage or healing, and creates neither Wounds nor resource triggers. A structural progression change without its adapter instead makes the restore unavailable. |
| An ally began with a6-point Soul Cage shield, later lost it, and the original grant remains valid. | The same shield returns with its snapshot6 points. The Soul Charge paid for it remains spent. This is not a new cast, grant or recipient offer. |
| Oracle A uses Time Loop. Before A's next actual regular turn, Oracle B uses it too. | Both Oracles retain their Reaction debts. Rewinding does not clear A's debt. Each debt clears only at that Oracle's genuine normal Reaction refresh. |
| A restored enemy dies again after its reward opportunity was already claimed. | That same reward cannot be claimed again. The source opportunity, rather than the new death event, determines whether it was paid. |
| A body part was harvested after initiative and still exists as somebody else's item. | The generic restore is unavailable: it cannot duplicate the body part or take away the current owner's item. A specifically reviewed reconciliation would be required. |
| An ally saw a hidden passage in the discarded timeline; another ally never learned about it. | The witness can retain that memory if eligible through the invoking Oracle's snapshot alliance. The other ally receives no automatic knowledge. The witness can tell them normally. |

An unavailable restore spends neither the Reaction nor the long-rest entitlement. The Director needs a complete, legal proposed state before resolving the ability; unresolved source interactions cannot be waived by calling a snapshot complete.

## Required integrations still missing

The minimum seventeen-domain review is not complete. Seven major integrations are unimplemented: actual concentration/transformation callbacks; Druid form and conserved recharge clocks; creature lifecycle/corpse/persistent assets; device lifecycle/stock/commands; remaining structures, Choir and control lifecycles; the complete FeatWorld; and source-qualified control/healing pulses. Even the implemented foundational domains are bounded by the input policies above. For example, the external concentration map is a dependency projection, not the callback-bearing live concentration adapter.

`TemporalKernel.support_report()` reports that limit. `playable_plan()` always rejects until the full implementation and independent review exist. `kernel_plan()` is a development fixture interface, not a replacement for the complete Oracle feature. The host must disclose every active integration. A supplied unsupported holder rejects preflight; an empty registration is not a certificate that a real game scene is complete.

`TemporalHealingCommitLedger` can be passed as the one canonical healing ledger to existing helpers. Its canonical return IDs preserve `FeatWorld.commit_healing` removal semantics, while its historical consumption tokens are iteration-qualified. Capture/preflight validate the live registry independently of `register()`: exact source/identity/absolute clock, canonical owner/target, boolean availability, and matching consumption-token/event history. External effect dictionary keys, effect identities, dependency identities and max-HP record identities must also agree. Agony creation/refresh/removal still needs the full feat adapter to synchronize active records; this kernel does not claim that synchronization exists.

## Validation and next review

Run `tools/validate_temporal_playtests.py`. The current suite contains 76 adversarial test methods. [Validation report](TEMPORAL_KERNEL_VALIDATION.json) records the tested helper hash. The initial 46-test packet, later 52-test packet, and [six independent findings](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_KERNEL_FINDINGS.md) are preserved separately. The notebook [confirmed the original six repairs](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_KERNEL_REPAIR_REVIEW.md), then identified three narrow identity/admission gaps. Those repairs and six additional test methods received [actual independent closure](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_KERNEL_FOUNDATION_CLOSURE.md). The [review status](TEMPORAL_KERNEL_REVIEW_STATUS.json) binds that disposition to the exact helper hash; the originally submitted helper is preserved in the audit archive; the later extension has its own review manifest. Two invented maximum-HP source examples in the first review already fail the existing source constructor; the exact temporal table additionally rejects actual valid sources lacking a temporal policy.

Next, add the seven missing integrations and exact source policies, with their own independent reviews. Do not remove the Time Loop deferred status based on these tests. The final joint whole-game flow review and authorized GitHub push remain later gates.

The subsequent [control/pulse conference and first implementation bridges](TEMPORAL_CONTROL_PLAYTEST.md) have their own recorded scope: nine source-policy families discussed,22 payment/output checks and50 bounded live-holder transaction methods jointly reviewed. Full nine-family restoration remains unfinished, so the seven missing-integration count is unchanged.

The next [form/concentration parent policies](TEMPORAL_PARENT_PLAYTEST.md) are now source-discussed with the notebook, including all26 Druid profiles and explicit renewal/stabilization history. The [parent status](TEMPORAL_PARENT_REVIEW_STATUS.json) records ten cases and the corrected Action-budget wording. Runtime parent integration and its validation are still pending.

The [exact-parent reference transport extension](TEMPORAL_REFERENCE_TRANSACTION_REVIEW_STATUS.json) is now jointly reviewed:15 new checks plus the existing207 pass. The prior control-checkpoint foundation is preserved at `docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/temporal_playtest_rules_control_checkpoint.py`; the current kernel hash has its own explicit review manifest. Only identity transport/rollback is added. Active form admission and full parent restoration remain gated.

**Principle:** Stagnation forbidden — geography shifts, rivers reverse, settlements migrate.

currentOperational.targets: One living creature you can perceive within range and line of effect
currentOperational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute; ends when its prevention is used
currentOperational.resolution: No initial save. While the spell remains active, the first eligible effect that would reduce the target from positive HP to 0 without Core Instant Death or another outright-death result instead leaves it at 1 HP; then the ward ends.
currentOperational.effect: Prevent one positive-to-zero HP crossing. Preserve the raw damage packet, Core Instant Death check, half-maximum/Maiming Wound triggers and attached conditions. The prevented positive-to-zero crossing does not itself create a drop-only Wound save. This is loss prevention, not healing, so a cannot-regain-HP effect does not stop it. Other eligible survival effects are rechecked after the selected prevention resolves; no duplicate automatic use is consumed after the crossing has already been prevented.
currentOperational.scaling: None. Always one eligible crossing and a 1-HP floor.
currentOperational.limitations: Does not trigger while the target is already at 0. Does not resurrect, repair a vital body, prevent third death-save failure/fatal Wound death/lethal-track death or override explicitly unpreventable HP loss. Cannot legalize an otherwise unaffordable HP cost. If multiple independently owned wards exist, use only the chosen eligible prevention; unused records retain their own concentration/deadline. This is distinct from Cleric Ritual of Undeath's would-die replacement. Normal spell costs and risk apply.
currentOperational.designNotes: Core Necromancy rank4, 7RP, Action, 60ft and concentration1minute retained with exact class gates. M/F uses the already-reviewed class-focus alternative; no unstated material cost. NEW: living target, explicit positive crossing, outright-death exclusion and competing-prevention procedure. The agreed damage/HP-loss interface is in the candidate guide; reviewed for the operational playtest overlay.

currentCard.name: Ritual of Undeath
currentCard.rangeAndTarget: One eligible corpse within 30 feet or one living ally within 30 feet
currentCard.effect: Ritual of Undeath. Tags: cultist, undead, rite. Choose one mode. Corpse Servant: one humanoid corpse dead no more than 1 minute rises for 3 rounds as a temporary thrall with AC 13, 10 HP, Speed 30 feet and one attack only when you spend your shared companion Bonus Action command using your Cleric technique attack bonus; on hit it deals S d6 necrotic. The thrall disappears at 0 HP or when duration ends and grants no XP, loot, new corpse, Conviction or resurrection target. Death Ward: one living ally is marked for 1 minute; the first time it would die during that duration, it instead remains at 1 HP and counts as both humanoid and undead until the end of its next turn. Neither mode removes Wounds. The Conviction expenditure can vent Dissonance once.

coreDamageDeath.excerpt:
Resolve each genuinely separate hit or damage event once. Do not split one packet to multiply Wound saves or combine separate hits merely to cross a threshold. Feature-specific prevention that acts before damage or before reaching zero resolves at its printed timing first.

1. Resolve attack/save, damage and applicable defenses. The remaining nonnegative amount is **resolved damage**.
2. Record HP, Wounds and zero-HP state before the event. Remove temporary HP first. **Post-temp damage = resolved damage minus temporary HP absorbed.** Keep this amount even when it exceeds current HP; floor the resulting current HP at zero.
3. Check V6 Instant Death. If post-temp damage minus HP before the hit is at least maximum HP, the creature dies. For a creature already at zero, this is post-temp damage at least maximum HP. Stop: there is no Wound save, death-save failure or successful knockout from that event.
4. Otherwise, a living creature makes one Wound save if it dropped from positive HP to zero, if **2 × post-temp damage is at least maximum HP**, or if the effect actually inflicts Maiming. Overlapping triggers still cause only one save. The post-temp threshold and one-save rule are new provisional interpretations. Maiming is an independent trigger even when temporary HP absorbs all ordinary damage; immunity to Maiming itself still applies.
5. Make a Constitution save against **max(10, floor(post-temp damage / 2))**. Use pre-event Wounds for the -1-per-Wound penalty. Maiming with zero post-temp damage uses DC 10. A Wound gained now cannot penalize the roll that created it.
6. A success adds no Wound. A failure that began with zero, one or two Wounds adds exactly one; failure by 5 or more also gives that Wound one Injury. A failure that began with three Wounds kills the creature instead: no fourth Wound and no Injury roll. Stop processing later living-target consequences if dead.
7. If the creature was already at zero before this event and post-temp damage is positive, end Stable. A creature using death saves adds one failure, or two for a critical hit; three failures kill it. An ordinary creature that does not use death saves dies instead, without starting death counters. A hit from positive HP to zero does not also cause a same-packet death failure.
8. If this event newly reduces positive HP to zero, a valid melee knockout makes the surviving creature Stable. Otherwise a character/significant NPC using death saves begins dying; an ordinary monster dies. A previously Stable creature whose temporary HP absorbed all damage remains Stable unless an independent Maiming result killed it. The Director identifies significant NPCs consistently. Knockout cannot override Instant Death or a fatal Wound save.

coreTaskDegrees.excerpt:
**Task, skill or tool check against a fixed DC:** total at least DC+10 is Critical Success; at least DC is Success; at most DC-10 is Critical Failure; other totals below DC are Failure. Natural 20 then improves one degree and natural 1 worsens one, bounded at either end. A task printing only success/failure collapses the two upper degrees to success and two lower degrees to failure; no extra consequence is invented. A natural 20 can still fail an otherwise impossible check, and a natural 1 with sufficient modifiers can still succeed.

**Saving throw:** total at least DC succeeds; otherwise it fails. Natural 1 and 20 have no generic special outcome. A printed failure by 5 or 10 compares the final total with the DC; it does not add an unprinted critical-save system. Death saves are the specific exception below.

dazed.excerpt:
## Dazed

**Preserved Core text:** Choose either action or movement on the turn, not both; no bonus action.

**Effect:** On every affected turn, including extra turns, choose Action-mode (at most one Action total and no voluntary Speed expenditure or Dash) or Movement-mode (ordinary movement, no Action). Movement expressly included in the permitted Action still resolves. No Bonus Action; Reactions and concentration are unaffected.

**Application:** Only an effect that explicitly inflicts Dazed applies it.

**Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's endpoint. Applies immediately: earlier voluntary movement that turn forbids further Actions; an earlier Action forbids further voluntary Speed expenditure; if both already occurred, neither may occur again. Do not undo completed events. Extra-Action grants cannot bypass the one-Action ceiling.

**Stacking:** Multiple Dazed applications do not further reduce the turn; track only the longest/independent ending sources.

**Immunities and specific exceptions:** An immunity to Dazed blocks application. Forced movement is not voluntary movement and remains possible.

currentOperational.targets: One willing creature you can perceive within range and line of effect, including yourself.
currentOperational.duration: 1 hour: expires 3,600 seconds after application. Initiative entry, exit or reorder does not reset this deadline.
currentOperational.effect: The target has advantage on saving throws against effects explicitly identified as Corruption by their current canonical mechanical source. This advantage can apply to each qualifying save while the ward lasts.
currentOperational.limitations: Does not invent a save for an effect that grants none, cure or lower existing Corruption, remove a curse, or grant immunity. Theme, ancestry, appearance, alignment and faction are not Corruption tags. Advantage never stacks. Known/prepared access, class-level gates, legal components, line of effect, payment before resolution, concentration transitions, Dissonance, Refrain and class cadence follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. No automatic scaling or generic upcast. Only one Corruption Ward can be active on a target across all casters. A later application replaces the previous ward with its own 3,600-second deadline; stale cleanup of the old application cannot remove the replacement.
currentOperational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action, 30 feet, 1 hour and advantage against Corruption; M/F uses the existing class-focus alternative. NEW: willing target, exact source-tag eligibility and elapsed deadline.
